comparisons.reason: Both are any-comment binary features over OC_comments, but the constructs differ in breadth. Feature 0 counts only a specific, verifiable procedural example, meaning a concrete description of an actual procedure, process, rule, protocol or practice, such as how a legal or institutional process works. Feature 1 counts any concrete real-world example: a case, event, person, organization, historical episode or personal experience. A person, event or personal anecdote with no procedural element would score 1 on feature 1 and 0 on feature 0. Feature 1 is therefore broader, and feature 0 is a narrower subtype. Their handling of OP quotes and empty or null lists is similar, but that does not offset the difference in eligibility.
